title: The Flagship's Flaw
logline: A disgraced veteran hires a pilot to scan a famous shipwreck and prove their innocence, but the veterans' association will pay anything to keep the official history intact.

roles.description: Exiled and aging, obsessed with clearing their name before they die.
Powerful and well-connected, fiercely protects the official history of the war.
The silent, picked-over skeleton of an old flagship drifting in deep space.
Sells coordinates to old wrecks, doesn't care about the history attached to them.
A heavy interceptor flying without transponders, loyal to the association.
A seedy listening post on the edge of the system.

public_situation: The local {role:veterans_association} is preparing a memorial for the anniversary of a famous victory. The {role:disgraced_veteran} is publicly banned from attending.
private_truth: The veteran didn't flee the battle; they were ordered to fall back because the flagship's reactor was failing. The association covered up the flagship's flaw to protect a lucrative shipyard contract.

beats.public_change: The veteran is publicly thrown out of a station lounge for trying to talk about the battle.

missions.reason: The veteran is banned from the trade docks and needs a pilot to retrieve a datacard with the exact coordinates of the flagship's wreck from the salvage broker.
missions.private_fact: The broker knows the association has a bounty on these coordinates and is trying to stall the pilot until the enforcers arrive.

beats.public_change: Association ships begin patrolling the outer system, claiming it is for 'memorial security'.

missions.reason: The veteran needs a pilot to fly to the wreck and scan the flagship's reactor housing for outward-burst damage to prove it failed from the inside.
missions.private_fact: The pilot must choose whether to certify the true reactor failure, or falsify the report to say it was combat damage as the association claims.

beats.public_change: The veteran prepares to publicly broadcast the scan results to the entire system.

missions.reason: An association ship moves to intercept the pilot on their way back with the scan data. The veteran begs the pilot to fight them off and deliver the proof.
missions.private_fact: The enforcer hails the pilot mid-fight, offering a massive 'consulting fee' from the association to delete the data and walk away.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot destroys the enforcer and delivers the scan data.
resolutions.summary: The data is published. The association faces a massive scandal over the cover-up, and the veteran's name is cleared.

consequences.public_summary: Someone dragged up proof that the old flagship blew its own reactor, and the brass lied about it.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot certifies false combat damage or takes the association's payout.
resolutions.summary: The association's official history remains unquestioned. The veteran is completely discredited as a liar and leaves the system in disgrace.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot apparently found the old flagship wreck and let the association scrub the nav-logs.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot ignores the veteran's request or abandons the job.
resolutions.summary: The association finds the wreck first and completely melts the reactor housing. The veteran dies broke and dishonored.

loose_threads.detail: The association recently bought up the salvage rights for the entire sector just to keep anyone from flying out there.
The scorch marks on the reactor housing were made by a modern industrial cutter, not combat lasers.

radio_hooks: {role:veterans_association} preparing for massive memorial service this week.
Local veteran arrested again for disturbing the peace at the trade docks.

voice_direction.disgraced_veteran: Raspy, exhausted, speaks with intense, unblinking sincerity.
voice_direction.salvage_broker: Fast, nervous, always sounds like they are checking over their shoulder.
